subject: math

hotspots.label: Zero reference
hotspots.description: Zero is the reference point at the center of the line, where positive numbers on the right meet negative numbers on the left.
hotspots.positionHint: The center tick on the line, larger and labeled 0.
hotspots.function: Zero is the reference point separating positive and negative number regions.

hotspots.label: Positive numbers
hotspots.description: Positive numbers live right of zero and get larger the further right you go.
hotspots.positionHint: The half of the line to the right of 0, labeled 1 through 5.
hotspots.function: Numbers to the right of zero, increasing in value.

hotspots.label: Negative numbers
hotspots.description: Negative numbers live left of zero and get smaller the further left you go.
hotspots.positionHint: The half of the line to the left of 0, labeled −1 through −5.
hotspots.function: Numbers left of zero, representing amounts below zero.

hotspots.label: Equal tick spacing
hotspots.description: Every tick is the same distance apart, which is what lets the line measure true jumps and distances.
hotspots.positionHint: A short length marker spanning two consecutive ticks above the right half of the line.
hotspots.function: Equal gaps make the line a true measuring ruler for number steps.

visualStyleNotes: Math palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no scene props. A single clean horizontal number line floats centered and large in frame. Soft neutral studio light, no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive. The line is a thin matte cylinder with short perpendicular tick posts and small number labels rendered as flat plates. Strong saturated color reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (ink / violet / grid-blue accents from the Math palette). Specimen-quality clean-3D, not cartoon, not gamey. Slow auto-rotation is subtle (the model is a thin line so rotation stays gentle).
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K texture-less material set. Line body: warm neutral off-white matte (roughness ~0.55). Tick marks: soft ink-grey (roughness ~0.5). Jump marker arrow: warm amber with a faint satin sheen (roughness ~0.4). Number label plates: warm paper white with ink-grey glyph text. No emissive channels anywhere — any highlight or glow on interaction is handled by app runtime UI, not baked in.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a single procedural horizontal number line built to read as 'a movable ruler for numbers.' Clean primitives, no downloaded mesh.

GEOMETRY: a thin center cylinder along the x-axis (length ~3.3, radius ~0.02) centered at origin. Perpendicular tick marks are small upright boxes spaced evenly at x = −2.5..2.5 at 0.5 steps (so 11 marks for −5..5). The zero mark is slightly taller/brighter to read as a reference. Number labels (−5 through 5) are thin flat plates facing the camera just above each tick. A small spherical marker + short arrow stub hangs on the jump control so the app can slide it to any tick.

LAYERS (toggleable): (1) Numeric labels on/off; (2) jump arrow + marker overlay; (3) equal-spacing gauge (a short double-arrow spanning two ticks).

CAMERA: default framing head-on (from the +z axis) so the whole −5..5 span fits with margin; auto-rotate wiggle is very slow so labels stay legible. Budget 4-8k triangles. Named nodes: Line_Body, Ticks, Label_Plates, Jump_Marker, Jump_Arrow, SpacingGauge, Zero_Tick, PositiveHalf, NegativeHalf. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
